input.quote: Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party. Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement
input.rationale: Paragraph 4(a) is the only convenience-termination provision (no Exhibit or other clause supplements it; there is no separate prepaid-fee or early-termination-fee mechanic). It sits at the playbook fallback rather than the preferred position: (i) the committed period is a single 1-year Initial Term (not a multi-year lock-in), so the absence of a convenience right during that 12-month period does not trigger the "term longer than 12 months" deviation test; (ii) after the Initial Term we may terminate for any reason on ninety (90) days' notice, at the outer edge of the 60–90 day fallback window; and (iii) Vendor's (Kubient's) convenience right is symmetrical and available only following the Initial Term on ninety (90) days' notice, which matches the fallback (end-of-term only, 90 days) and is not the walk-away case of Vendor exit on fewer than 90 days or mid-term. Kubient's entitlement to fees generated during the 90-day notice period is payment for services actually delivered in that window and in any event does not exceed the fallback's 3-months'-fees ceiling. Noted but not flagged as a deviation: there is no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on termination, and no ability to terminate individual Exhibits/Order Forms in part — both sub-elements of the preferred position we can raise as drafting comments if this clause is reopened.
